text: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak tenderly to Jerusalem and announce to her that her hard service is over, her guilt is paid, and she has received double for all her sins.
A voice cries out: Clear the LORD's way in the wilderness; make a straight highway for our God in the desert.
Every valley will be lifted up, and every mountain and hill will be leveled; the uneven ground will become smooth and the rugged land a plain.
Then the glory of the LORD will appear, and all humanity together will see it, for the LORD's mouth has spoken.
A voice says, Cry out. And I said, What should I cry out? All humanity is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the LORD blows on it; indeed, the people are grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.
Zion, herald of good news, go up on a high mountain. Jerusalem, herald of good news, raise your voice loudly; lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the cities of Judah, Here is your God!
Look, the Lord GOD comes with strength, and his power establishes his rule. His reward is with him, and his gifts accompany him.
He protects his flock like a shepherd; he gathers the lambs in his arms and carries them in the fold of his garment; he gently leads the nursing ewes.
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off the heavens with a ruler, gathered the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains on scales?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or as his counselor has taught him?
Who did he consult? Who gave him understanding? Who taught him the path of justice or taught him knowledge or showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket; they are considered as a speck of dust on a scale; he lifts up the islands like fine dust.
Lebanon's forest is not enough fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before him; they are considered by him as empty and nothing.
To whom will you compare God? What likeness will you set alongside him?
As for an idol, a craftsman casts it, a metalworker plates it with gold and fashions silver chains for it.
A poor person, unable to afford an offering, chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not fall over.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Was it not told to you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth's foundations were laid?
God is enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; he stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He brings rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth meaningless.
They are barely planted, barely sown, their stem hardly rooted, when he blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind carries them off like stubble.
To whom will you compare me, or who is my equal? asks the Holy One.
Look up and see: who created these stars? He brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; because of his great power and might, not one of them is missing.
Why do you say, Jacob, and complain, Israel: My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, creator of the ends of the earth; he does not grow tired or weary, and his understanding is beyond searching out.
He gives strength to the weary and strengthens the powerless.
Youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall,
but those who wait on the LORD will renew their strength; they will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
